column4: A product card on our page groups an image, a title and a price that we style and script together with the rest of the page. Should the card be a div or an iframe?

We must show a partner's separately hosted booking page inside our page. Its styles must not leak into ours, and it uses no camera, location or other device features. Should we use a div or an iframe?
Our help articles are separate HTML documents, but each one must look like part of the page, share our styles and be read in the same accessibility tree. Should the article go in a div or an iframe?
We must show a partner's separately hosted video call page inside our page, isolated from our styles, and the call needs the camera. Should we use a div or an iframe?
We want to show some help content on the page and it should match our styles. Should we use a div or an iframe?
Write the installation instructions: download the archive, unpack it, then run the installer. Doing them in another order breaks the install. Should this be an ol or a ul?
List the ingredients of a salad; the reader can gather them in any order. Should this be an ol or a ul?
Show the ten best-selling books of the week, where the position of each book is its rank. Should this be an ol or a ul?
Show the links of the site footer: about, contact, privacy and careers; their order carries no meaning. Should this be an ol or a ul?
Make a list of things for the party. Should this be an ol or a ul?

One page needs a three-line classic script that sets the copyright year. No other page uses it, there is no Content Security Policy, and it may run where it appears. Inline code or an external file with src?
Every page of the site needs the same classic script that sets the copyright year. There is no Content Security Policy, and it may run where it appears. Inline code or an external file with src?

One page needs a short classic script, and the site sends a Content Security Policy whose script-src does not include 'unsafe-inline'. We can add files to the site. Inline code or an external file with src?

One page needs a short classic script, the site sends a Content Security Policy whose script-src does not include 'unsafe-inline', and the hosting does not let us add any new file. How should the script be included?
A classic script in the head must run only after the whole document is parsed, before other deferred scripts that come later, and we can put it in its own file. How should it be included?

A classic script in the head must run only after the whole document is parsed, but it has to stay inline because we cannot add files. Someone suggests adding defer to the inline script. How should it be included?
Our script is a JavaScript module that imports other modules, it must run after the document is parsed, and we can put it in its own file. Do we also need defer?
